CHIEF COMPLAINT
Rash that is improving but not fully resolved

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports that her rash is doing much better and under good control. She has a small amount of rash leftover. She was initially taking doxycycline twice daily and noticed a lot of improvement. Last week, she reduced to once daily on advice from her pharmacist, thinking that since the rash was getting better she should limit it. However, since reducing to once daily, the improvement has plateaued and it is not continuing to get better. She stopped breastfeeding prior to starting doxycycline. She was hesitant to use elidel initially after reading about it but has agreed to consider other options. She is currently using sulfacetamide wash twice daily and metro cream applied after face washing. She denies using other lotions, cetaphil cleanser, or neutrogena wipes. She reports feeling sun sensitive when going outside and takes precautions including wearing a hat.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Perioral dermatitis, rosacea including ocular rosacea

MEDICATIONS
Sulfacetamide wash twice daily
Metro cream applied after face wash
Doxycycline (recently reduced to once daily)

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient recently stopped breastfeeding. Reports sun sensitivity and uses protective measures including hats when outdoors.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Fitzpatrick skin type IV (will tan, not burn). Bilateral medial cheeks with a few faint erythematous papules and mild redness around and underneath nostrils. Rash not completely resolved.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Perioral dermatitis, rosacea including ocular rosacea. Continue sulfacetamide wash once daily. Continue metro cream. Increase doxycycline back to twice daily until rash is gone, then once daily for another week before stopping. Patient to start tacrolimus ointment applied to rash area twice daily until resolved. Advised about potential side effects of doxycycline including upset stomach, heartburn, and increased sun sensitivity. Discussed that tacrolimus may cause brief tingling or needle-like sensation or redness for a few seconds after application. Recommended basic moisturizer such as vanicream or petroleum jelly. Patient to avoid steroids on face. Once rash stops, can discontinue tacrolimus but continue doxycycline for another week then stop. Continue using wash and metro cream. Hold off on old products until follow-up visit. If rash flares slightly, can try tacrolimus alone for a couple days; if not improving, restart doxycycline. If rash worsens rather than improves, patient should call or send MyChart message. Recommend gentle eyelid washing once daily with gentle cleanser such as vanicream and use Bruder mask as needed. Follow-up appointment scheduled in about four weeks. Patient has adequate refills of current medications.
